{
  "dataset_name": "phoneme",
  "model_family": "tree",
  "schema_generator": "claude-sonnet-4.6",
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "features": [
    {
      "name": "spectral_energy_sum",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Sum of all five spectral coefficients representing total spectral energy across frequency bands",
      "formula": "V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5",
      "value_range": [-6.586, 15.241],
      "feature_family": "aggregation",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures overall spectral magnitude which may differ systematically between phoneme groups",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "spectral_peak_value",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Maximum spectral coefficient value across all five bands indicating dominant frequency component",
      "formula": "np.maximum(np.maximum(np.maximum(np.maximum(V1, V2), V3), V4), V5)",
      "value_range": [-1.145, 3.773],
      "feature_family": "aggregation",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Peak spectral energy is a strong discriminator for phoneme classification trees to split on",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "spectral_range",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Difference between maximum and minimum spectral coefficients measuring spectral spread",
      "formula": "np.maximum(np.maximum(np.maximum(np.maximum(V1, V2), V3), V4), V5) - np.minimum(np.minimum(np.minimum(np.minimum(V1, V2), V3), V4), V5)",
      "value_range": [0.0, 6.515],
      "feature_family": "spread",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Spectral spread distinguishes phonemes with concentrated vs distributed frequency energy",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "low_freq_to_high_freq_ratio",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ratio of low frequency bands (V1+V2) to high frequency bands (V4+V5) capturing spectral tilt",
      "formula": "(V1 + V2) / (np.abs(V4 + V5) + 0.001)",
      "value_range": [-15.0, 50.0],
      "feature_family": "ratio",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Spectral tilt ratio provides nonlinear interaction between frequency bands useful for tree splits",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "mid_band_dominance",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Whether V3 (mid-frequency band) exceeds the mean of V1 and V5 (edge bands), indicating mid-frequency dominance",
      "formula": "np.where(V3 > (V1 + V5) / 2.0, 1, 0)",
      "value_range": [0, 1],
      "feature_family": "boolean_indicator",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Boolean split on mid-frequency dominance creates direct threshold for tree models",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "spectral_gradient_v1_v5",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Linear slope from V1 to V5 measuring spectral trend direction across frequency bands",
      "formula": "(V5 - V1) / 4.0",
      "value_range": [-1.229, 1.019],
      "feature_family": "gradient",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Spectral slope direction and magnitude helps trees identify rising vs falling spectral patterns",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "v2_v3_interaction",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Product of V2 and V3 capturing nonlinear interaction between adjacent mid-frequency bands",
      "formula": "V2 * V3",
      "value_range": [-3.5, 10.9],
      "feature_family": "interaction",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Multiplicative interaction creates curved decision boundaries that tree ensembles can approximate with splits",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "high_energy_band_count",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Count of spectral bands exceeding value 1.0 indicating number of high-energy frequency components",
      "formula": "np.where(V1 > 1.0, 1, 0) + np.where(V2 > 1.0, 1, 0) + np.where(V3 > 1.0, 1, 0) + np.where(V4 > 1.0, 1, 0) + np.where(V5 > 1.0, 1, 0)",
      "value_range": [0, 5],
      "feature_family": "ordinal_bucket",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Ordinal count of high-energy bands provides natural tree splits at integer thresholds",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "spectral_variance_proxy",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Variance proxy computed as mean squared deviation of each band from their collective mean",
      "formula": "((V1 - (V1+V2+V3+V4+V5)/5.0)**2 + (V2 - (V1+V2+V3+V4+V5)/5.0)**2 + (V3 - (V1+V2+V3+V4+V5)/5.0)**2 + (V4 - (V1+V2+V3+V4+V5)/5.0)**2 + (V5 - (V1+V2+V3+V4+V5)/5.0)**2) / 5.0",
      "value_range": [0.0, 8.5],
      "feature_family": "spread",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Spectral variance captures uniformity vs peakedness of frequency distribution for tree splitting",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "v1_negative_indicator",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Boolean indicator for negative V1 values which may signal atypical low-frequency spectral behavior",
      "formula": "np.where(V1 < 0.0, 1, 0)",
      "value_range": [0, 1],
      "feature_family": "boolean_indicator",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Direct boolean split on V1 sign provides a simple but potentially powerful tree node",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "spectral_energy_bucket",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Ordinal bucket (0-3) representing overall spectral energy level: 0=very low (sum<0), 1=low (0 to 2), 2=medium (2 to 5), 3=high (sum>=5)",
      "value_range": [0, 3],
      "feature_family": "ordinal_bucket",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Discretized energy level creates clean categorical splits for tree models without numeric noise",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "spectral_shape_type",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Categorical shape encoding: 0=monotone decreasing (V1>V2>V3>V4>V5), 1=monotone increasing (V1<V2<V3<V4<V5), 2=peaked in middle (V3 is max), 3=other irregular shape",
      "value_range": [0, 3],
      "feature_family": "categorical_grouping",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Spectral shape type groups phonemes by frequency profile pattern enabling categorical splits in trees",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    }
  ]
}
